statement: A doc that describes SHIPPED behaviour must state what the code does, not what an earlier draft of the plan proposed: when a planning document becomes the document of record, re-verify every specific claim (thresholds, intervals, mechanisms, flags) against the implementation and rewrite the ones that drifted.
rationale: David, 2026-09-17 (commit 3847af9): the shipped doc still claimed the hook 'skips entirely when the stored record is younger than 60 seconds'. That was a throttle proposed in the planning draft and never built; the implemented guard is `Date.now() - observed_at < 86_400_000 && sameWorkspaceContent(...)` — one day AND unchanged content. The same audit found a second survivor in the same paragraph ('detached spawn', a mechanism removed when the session-start child was dropped). A plan doc promoted to the document of record carries claims nobody re-checked, and a false claim about shipped behaviour is worse than no doc: it is doc-vs-code drift, exactly what this repository exists to prevent.
